children: Gold and silver reversed sharply lower Wednesday after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023 and signaled that additional tightening may still be needed, strengthening the dollar and putting fresh pressure on non-yielding precious metals.

The Fed unanimously raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a 3.75% to 4.00% range, matching market expectations. But the bigger surprise came from the policy outlook: 16 of 18 officials projected at least one additional rate increase before year-end.
December gold fell about 0.7% after hours to roughly $4,302 per ounce, while December silver slipped 0.6% to $63.42.
That erased part of a strong regular-session rally. Front-month gold had gained 1.3% to $4,346.30, while silver climbed 1.6% to $64.288.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reinforced the hawkish interpretation by keeping the central bank's focus squarely on persistent inflation.

"Our predominant focus is on the price stability side of our mandate. The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has been for too long. This summer's inflation readings do not tell me that ?underlying trends have meaningfully improved," Warsh said.
The Fed's formal statement similarly said inflation remains elevated and that higher rates should support a quicker return toward its 2% target.
The immediate problem for precious metals is not Wednesday's quarter-point increase itself. Markets largely expected that.
The bigger issue is the prospect of another hike.
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding assets such as gold that produce no yield, while a stronger dollar can make metals more expensive for overseas buyers.
That creates a near-term test after both metals rallied strongly.

Investors should now watch inflation data, the dollar and expectations for the Fed's remaining 2026 meetings. If markets begin pricing an extended tightening cycle, gold and silver could face additional pressure.
But if inflation cools quickly enough to reduce expectations for further hikes, Wednesday's reversal could prove temporary rather than the start of a larger trend change.

title: Gold and Silver Just Sent Investors a Strong Signal
